title: Ego is a chronic illness with a cure inside it
subtitle: Raag Aasaa
summary: Guru Angad does not flatter ego or mystify it. He names it as the pattern behind action and bondage, then says the cure appears through grace and the Guru's Shabad.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who keeps locating every problem outside the self while anger, injury, and self-importance keep returning. Stay close to this shabad after conflict, and it turns self-diagnosis from shame into treatment.
takeaway: Treat ego as illness and keep the Guru's medicine near.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਏਹਾ ਜਾਤਿ ਹੈ ਹਉਮੈ ਕਰਮ ਕਮਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai ehaa jaat hai haumai karam kamaeh ||
lines.translation: This is the nature of ego, that people perform their actions in ego.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਏਈ ਬੰਧਨਾ ਫਿਰਿ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨੀ ਪਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai eiee ba(n)dhanaa fir fir jonee paeh ||
lines.translation: This is the bondage of ego, that time and time again, they are reborn.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਕਿਥਹੁ ਊਪਜੈ ਕਿਤੁ ਸੰਜਮਿ ਇਹ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai kithahu uoopajai kit sa(n)jam ieh jai ||
lines.translation: Where does ego come from? How can it be removed?

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਏਹੋ ਹੁਕਮੁ ਹੈ ਪਇਐ ਕਿਰਤਿ ਫਿਰਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai eho hukam hai piaai kirat firaeh ||
lines.translation: This ego exists by the Lord's Order; people wander according to their past actions.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਦੀਰਘ ਰੋਗੁ ਹੈ ਦਾਰੂ ਭੀ ਇਸੁ ਮਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: haumai dheeragh rog hai dhaaroo bhee is maeh ||
lines.translation: Ego is a chronic disease, but it contains its own cure as well.

lines.gurmukhi: ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰੇ ਜੇ ਆਪਣੀ ਤਾ ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਕਮਾਹਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: kirapaa kare je aapanee taa gur kaa sabadh kamaeh ||
lines.translation: If the Lord grants His Grace, one acts according to the Teachings of the Guru's Shabad.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕੁ ਕਹੈ ਸੁਣਹੁ ਜਨਹੁ ਇਤੁ ਸੰਜਮਿ ਦੁਖ ਜਾਹਿ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: naanak kahai sunahu janahu it sa(n)jam dhukh jaeh ||2||
lines.translation: Nanak says, listen, people: in this way, troubles depart. ||2||

structure: The shabad begins by naming ego as the force behind ordinary action and repeated bondage.
From there it asks the decisive question: where does ego arise, and how does it leave?
The closing movement rests by locating the cure in grace and in living the Guru's Shabad.
